title: Command dragging a clip's edge ripple trims, so later clips follow
goal: Trimming the end of a clip by dragging its edge leaves a gap that then has to be closed by hand. In Premiere, holding Command while dragging an edge with the selection tool makes it a ripple trim: the clips after it slide along so no gap opens. Give Photonz the same drag, so tightening a cut by eye is one gesture.
notes: Found by the manager's Premiere check on 2026-10-16: an edge drag never ripples (Sources/PhotonzCore/ClipPieces.swift:860-874, 909-918; ClipBarDrag.swift:41-52 has no modifier handling; EditorState+ClipBar.swift:567-569 leaves the next clip in place). Q and W already ripple to the playhead (RippleTrim.swift:71-84), so reuse their all-tracks shift rather than a second ripple. Premiere on the Mac: with the Selection tool, holding Command over an edit point gives the Ripple Edit cursor (third-party guides, not Adobe docs; check Adobe's own help before shipping and cite it in the audit). Rolling a cut by drag (Premiere's N) is not this task. TDD for the Core part.
acceptance: Holding Command while dragging a clip's end edge moves every later clip on every unlocked track by the same amount, closing or opening time, as one undo; a plain drag behaves exactly as today
Holding Command while dragging a clip's start edge trims its head and pulls the clip and everything after it left so the clip keeps its place's start, as Premiere's ripple trim does
The edge shows Premiere's ripple look while Command is held over it (a different pointer or a tinted edge), and snapping still works during the drag
Try path, no flag changed from Next defaults: on the sample recording with two pieces, hold Command and drag the first piece's end edge left; the second piece follows

Audit written under queue/audits/ naming Premiere's modifier it follows; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
